name: Systemic Mastocytosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO 2022 Classification / ICC Criteria for Systemic Mastocytosis

criteria.description: Multifocal dense infiltrates of mast cells (>=15 mast cells in aggregates) on bone marrow biopsy and/or other extracutaneous organ(s)
>25% of mast cells in bone marrow or other extracutaneous organ are spindle-shaped or have atypical morphology
KIT D816V point mutation or other activating KIT mutation in bone marrow, blood, or other extracutaneous organ
Mast cells in bone marrow or blood co-express CD25 and/or CD2 in addition to normal mast cell markers
Serum baseline tryptase persistently >20 ng/mL (does not apply if there is an associated hematologic neoplasm)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: 1 major + 1 minor criterion, OR 3 minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Further subclassified into indolent SM (ISM), smoldering SM (SSM), aggressive SM (ASM), SM with associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN), and mast cell leukemia. ISM is by far the most common subtype.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Urticaria pigmentosa / maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis with systemic involvement
pathognomonic.notes: Darier sign positive: urtication upon stroking a skin lesion

common.notes: Up to 50% of adults with SM who are stung experience severe anaphylaxis

occasional.symptomName: Hypotension or syncope during mediator release

occasional.notes: Most common cause of morbidity in ISM

laboratory: KIT D816V mutation in peripheral blood or bone marrow (>90% of cases)
CBC: may show eosinophilia; cytopenias in advanced disease
Alkaline phosphatase and LDH may be elevated in advanced disease
imaging: CT abdomen: hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy in advanced disease
Bone scan: osteosclerotic or osteolytic lesions in some cases
genetic: KIT D816V somatic activating mutation (>90% of cases)
Other KIT mutations at codon 816 or elsewhere (rare)
Additional mutations (TET2, SRSF2, ASXL1, RUNX1) in advanced SM
other: Bone marrow biopsy: multifocal mast cell aggregates, spindle-shaped mast cells, aberrant CD25/CD2 expression
Skin biopsy: increased dermal mast cells in cutaneous lesions
GI endoscopy with biopsy: increased mucosal mast cells

distinguishingFeatures: MCAS lacks clonal mast cell markers (no KIT D816V, no aberrant CD25)
MCAS has normal bone marrow mast cell morphology and number
SM has baseline tryptase >20 ng/mL and clonal markers
Cutaneous mastocytosis is limited to skin involvement
SM has extracutaneous (usually bone marrow) involvement
HaT has elevated tryptase from extra gene copies, not from clonal mast cells
HaT lacks KIT mutation and abnormal mast cell aggregates
Carcinoid has a neuroendocrine tumor on imaging

redFlags: Unexplained anaphylaxis (especially to Hymenoptera stings in adults)
Persistently elevated baseline serum tryptase >20 ng/mL
Organomegaly or cytopenias suggesting advanced disease
Unexplained osteoporosis in a young or middle-aged patient
Weight loss or B-symptoms (suggests aggressive SM or SM-AHN)
references: Valent P, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria and classification of mast cell disorders: a consensus proposal. Hemasphere. 2021;5(11):e646.
Pardanani A. Systemic mastocytosis in adults: 2021 update on diagnosis, risk stratification and management. Am J Hematol. 2021;96(4):508-525.

Gotlib J, et al. International Working Group-Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Research and Treatment (IWG-MRT) & European Competence Network on Mastocytosis (ECNM) consensus response criteria in advanced systemic mastocytosis. Blood. 2013;121(13):2393-2401.
